title: Equipment on site and planned maintenance
moduleTitle: App: Field service operations (proposed module; not in curriculum/structure yet)
audience: Owners and office staff who schedule, dispatch and record field jobs. No developer knowledge is needed.
learningOutcomes: Record equipment at a site as an asset, including parent and child items.
Set a recurring maintenance plan, giving it a repeat interval and a generation window.
Explain why a plan must be checked after an asset is replaced.

instruction.heading: Assets
instruction.body: An asset is a piece of equipment or a system at a customer's site that may need repeat service, such as an air conditioner, a pool pump or a commercial dishwasher. Recording assets gives each later job a history. An asset can sit under a parent, such as a plant room with several units beneath it. The reference guide sets limits on how large these groupings can grow.

instruction.heading: Maintenance plans
instruction.body: A maintenance plan sets how often visits should happen and creates jobs for future visits in batches. It has a start date, an optional end date that matches any contract, a job template, a customer and optionally a site. The frequency and its unit set the gap between visits. The generation window sets how far ahead jobs are created at one time. When a plan covers several assets, you decide between one job covering all of them or one job per asset. Assets lacking rules of their own inherit the plan's rules.

procedure: Record each asset at its site with its name, model and location notes.
Link child items to their parent where equipment sits inside another unit.
Set up the plan by entering its start date, optional end date and job template.
Set the frequency and the generation window.
Attach the assets covered and check which rules apply to each one.
After any replacement, update the asset record and check the plan points to the new unit.

workedExamples.situation: A strata building has a pool pump and a filter on the same plant. The client wants both serviced every three months.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you create one plan with two assets, or two plans?
workedExamples.reasoning: The frequency and template are the same, so one plan with both assets attached is simpler. The filter is linked as a child of the pump, so its service history stays with the equipment it serves.

equipmentAndPpe: A device with the Titan Zero Field app, where the lesson uses it

commonErrors.error: Replacing an asset by creating a new record but leaving the old one on the plan.
commonErrors.prevention: Retire the old asset and point the plan at the new one.

commonErrors.error: Setting a frequency without checking it against the contract's end date.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the plan's end date matches the contract term before saving.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson covers app records and office process only. It does not grant, confirm or replace any licence, certificate or authority, and it makes no legal claim.

qualityStandard: Each asset has a site link and a clear name.
Each maintenance plan has a frequency, a template and a generation window.
documentationEvidence: Asset register with site and installation notes
summary: Assets give each site its equipment history.
A maintenance plan creates future jobs in batches from a frequency.
Replacing equipment means updating both the asset and the plan.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is an asset in this app?
options: A worker's tool kit with the spare parts, the van stock and the bag
A piece of equipment at a customer site that may need repeat service
A customer's payment method on the account, the card and the bank

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants a visit every month. Which frequency setting fits?
What does the generation window control?
options: How far ahead jobs are created at one time
The price of each visit on the invoice
Which worker is paid for the visit
